sections.h2: Where Emmet County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Emmet County's Register of Deeds works from 200 Division Street, Suite 150, in Petoskey, MI 49770, and answers at 231-348-1761. Every deed for land in the county, from Harbor Springs to Pellston, ends up in this one office.

It handles more than 240 kinds of paper, including deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, leases, liens, probate orders, condominium documents and plats. The register also chairs the county plat board, which reviews new subdivisions.

Land records start in 1852. Images exist from that year forward, yet the name index only runs from 1922 on, with earlier years being added a little at a time. For older searches the county invites people in to use the index books at the counter.

sections.h2: Recording fees at the Petoskey counter
sections.html:
Recording starts at $30 per document, collected at the counter by cash or check only.

Emmet County register fee schedule
ServiceFee
Entering and recording any document$30
Warranty deeds, land contracts, covenant deeds and similar$35
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3 per instrument
Certification of a document$5
Tax certification, up to 5 descriptions$5
Each added description20 cents
Copies$1.00 a page in the office, $1.05 online

The $35 line applies to any deed carrying a warrant or covenant clause, and the $5 tax certification has to be added to that payment. By mail, write the check to the Emmet County Register of Deeds.

Every filing is measured against Michigan's recording statutes, and anything short is mailed back. These entries cause the most returns.

  • Signatures have to be originals with typed names under them, and the notary block must repeat those names exactly.
  • Keep a clear band of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch along every other edge.
  • Type in black ink, 10-point or bigger, on white stock of at least 20 pounds, cut anywhere from letter size to 8.5 by 14.
  • Put the name and address of whoever drafted the paper on anything signed in Michigan.
  • Show nothing beyond the final four digits of a Social Security number.
  • One instrument may cover only one recordable event.
  • Court orders come certified with the clerk's seal. A survivorship deed needs a certified death certificate recorded already.

Pack a return envelope with the filing. A paper is usually recorded the day it arrives, held for a day and mailed back the next business day, unless the title company or lender asked for something else.

sections.h2: How Emmet County transfer tax works
sections.html:
Michigan layers two taxes on the price. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 or part of $500 (MCL 207.525), and a county with under two million residents takes 55 cents on the same measure (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show the whole price, or carry an attached affidavit of value.

The register's downloads include a transfer tax table, a list of exemptions and a state refund application. Under MCL 207.502 and 207.523 the seller carries the bill.

Gifts running from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild escape the state tax under MCL 207.526, so long as the instrument states it. Ask the closer to show both taxes on the settlement statement so you can see what comes out of your proceeds.

Michigan uses a race-notice system. A recorded deed warns every later buyer, and papers rank in the order they were first handed in. First in time, first in line.

After closing, the deed and the buyer's mortgage should go straight to the register, since a delay lets a later filing cut ahead. Title companies know this and typically file the same day. In a private sale you would carry the deed in yourself or use an e-recording provider the county names: CSC, EPN or Simplifile.

The county page carries a ROD Alert about outside companies that offer certified copies of a deed for $50 or more. Copies cost as little as $1 a page at the register, and the office asks residents to call 231-348-1761 before paying a third party.

sections.h2: Searching Emmet County records for free
sections.html:
The online index is the quickest way to check your own chain of title before a sale. Searching works after a free registration. You can search by liber and page, by name or by document type, and a low-resolution preview shows before you pay $1.05 a page by card for a copy. The county also runs Fraud Notify, which sends an email each time a paper is recorded in your name.

Tax details sit in a separate property search on the county website that accepts a name, an address or a parcel number. Anyone buying or inheriting a house here should run both searches. If something on the record looks wrong, such as a mortgage that was paid off but never discharged, raise it with your title company early, since a clean record is what lets a closing go on schedule.

Emmet County sits at the tip of the Lower Peninsula, with Lake Michigan to the west and the Straits of Mackinac to the north. Petoskey holds the county seat and is the biggest city. Harbor Springs is the second city, and the villages are Alanson, Pellston and part of Mackinaw City.

It has 33,775 people sharing 22,395 housing units as of July 2025, and 15,190 households. Owners occupy 77.0% of the homes, and the median household income is $78,112. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $315,700.

The Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians hold at least 13 scattered reservation areas in the county, among them parts of Petoskey and several townships. A buyer or seller with a parcel near one should ask the title company how that land is treated.

Overdue taxes go through the county treasurer's office, which also issues the tax certification a deed needs before it can be recorded. The register will take redemption payments while the redemption period runs. After it ends, only the foreclosing unit can help.

A sale can wipe out the debt. The closer pays it from the proceeds and then orders the certification, so ask the treasurer for an exact payoff before you choose a closing day.

A short list of steps keeps the closing on track:

  1. Ask the treasurer for the exact payoff and whether the redemption period is still running.
  2. Give the figure to your closer so the certification can be ordered.
  3. Confirm the recording fee, with the extra $5 certification added for a warranty deed.
  4. Have the title company file the deed the same day, since the earliest filing ranks first.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the treasurer's certification and the recording rules above still apply to the deed.

faqs.q: Where is the Emmet County register's office?
faqs.a: 200 Division Street, Suite 150, Petoskey, MI 49770, phone 231-348-1761. Recording fees are paid in person by cash or check only.

faqs.q: What does a warranty deed cost to record in Emmet County?
faqs.a: $35. The county lists $30 as the base fee and puts warranty deeds, land contracts and other covenant-language deeds at $35, with the $5 tax certification folded into the payment.

faqs.q: Does Emmet County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, through three providers: CSC, EPN and Simplifile. Contact one of them for guidance on sending a deed in electronically.

faqs.q: How old are Emmet County land records?
faqs.a: They start in 1852. Images are indexed from 1922 forward and earlier indexing continues, so some older searches mean a trip to the index books.

faqs.q: Do Michigan deeds still need witnesses?
faqs.a: No. Witnesses are no longer required, though most documents still need a notary acknowledgment.
